brand_full_name: The University of Texas at Arlington
source_note: Seed profile from a quick first-pass sample (Mission page, an Admissions Apply page, a few instructional/FAQ pages), extended in seed-2 with rules from UTA's Marketing, Messaging, and Engagement Editorial Guidelines (https://www.uta.edu/administration/mme/brand-standards/editorial-guide). Not a full crawl-based profile -- broadening the sample is a deliberate later follow-up.

institutional.label: Institutional
institutional.description: Formal, third-person, no contractions, values-forward nouns ("collaboration," "excellence," "innovation," "integrity"). Sentences run longer and more compound.
institutional.example: The University is committed to providing access and ensuring student success, and to a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, and commercialization of discoveries by our community of scholars.

prospective_student.label: Prospective-student / service
prospective_student.description: Warm, second-person ("you," "you're"), plain and direct, occasional exclamation for encouragement, step-by-step instructional structure.
prospective_student.example: Applying for admission is easy at UTA and we're here to support you every step of the way!

shared_principles: Specific facts cited with sources rather than vague superlatives (e.g. citing U.S. News & World Report rather than saying "top-ranked")
seed_system_prompt: Detect or ask which register the target page calls for (institutional vs. prospective-student/service) and write in that register by default. Never let a requested tone (more casual, more formal, punchier) override UTA's baseline: no slang, no overclaiming, no unsourced superlatives, always plausible as something UTA's own Marketing, Messaging, and Engagement office would publish. Prefer concrete facts and sourced figures over generic marketing language. Second person is the default for anything audience-facing (admissions, current students, prospective students); third person for institutional/policy content.

guardrail.floor_description: Never generic AI copy that happens to be about UTA. No slang. No overclaiming. No unsourced superlatives. Always plausible as something UTA's own Marketing, Messaging, and Engagement office would publish. A requested tone adjustment (warmer, more formal, more concise, more detailed) changes style within a register -- it never lowers this floor.
checks: no unsourced superlative claims ("best," "top," "world-class") without a citable source
register consistency: institutional stays third-person/no-contractions, prospective-student stays second-person
no invented facts, statistics, or quotes not present in the source content

we_are.we_are: Supportive -- we walk people through what to do next
we_are.we_are_not: Hand-holding or patronizing -- support is concrete steps, not reassurance
we_are.evidence: Admissions page: "we're here to support you every step of the way"; FAQ/how-to pages are step-by-step. Confidence: medium (seed sample).

we_are.we_are_not: Boastful -- every claim of distinction carries its source
we_are.evidence: Shared principle: cite U.S. News & World Report rather than "top-ranked"; guardrail forbids unsourced superlatives. Confidence: high (explicit guidance).

we_are.we_are_not: Vague marketing copy that could describe any university
we_are.evidence: Guardrail floor: "Never generic AI copy that happens to be about UTA." Confidence: high (explicit guidance).

we_are.we_are_not: Slangy or casual-internet; also not academic jargon for a general reader
we_are.evidence: Shared principles; guardrail check "no slang or casual internet-speak." Confidence: high.

we_are.we_are: Committed to access and student success
we_are.evidence: Mission register example: "committed to providing access and ensuring student success." Confidence: medium (one source).

we_are.we_are: Rooted in North Texas -- the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex is part of who we are
we_are.evidence: University boilerplate: "Located in the heart of the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex..." (UTA News Center, 2025-01-10). Confidence: medium.

rewrite-page.note: Keep the source page's register; tone chips adjust within it.

new-page.note: Lead with what the reader can do or learn here.

program-page.note: Second person. Outcomes, requirements, and next steps before history.

landing-page.note: One goal, one primary call to action, short sections.

department-page.note: Institutional register: third person, no contractions.

compose-page.note: Plan the block sequence to match the request; lead with a hero.

news-story.note: AP style, inverted pyramid. News Center omits the serial comma.

event-announcement.note: What, when, where, who it's for, and how to register -- in the first two sentences.

press-release.note: Dateline, inverted pyramid, attributed quotes only if supplied, boilerplate last.

spotlight.note: Story-led; alumni get the degree citation after their name.

headlines.note: 60 characters or fewer; UTA or UT Arlington is fine in headlines.

meta-descriptions.note: 155 characters or fewer; say what the page lets the reader do.

ctas.note: Start with a verb; 2 to 5 words; say exactly what happens.

faq-set.note: Answer in the first sentence, then the detail.

summary.note: Keep every figure and requirement; drop everything else.

preferred.use: The University of Texas at Arlington
preferred.note: Full name on first reference, with a capital T in The.
Abbreviations take capital letters, no periods, no spaces.
Use No. in running text for rankings; # only in infographics.

style_rules: First reference: The University of Texas at Arlington. Later references and headlines: UTA, UT Arlington, or the University.
Capitalize University when it means UTA; lowercase it for universities in general.
Capitalize official names but not their parts: the Department of Mathematics, then the department.
Use the serial comma, except in News Center items (news stories and press releases), which follow AP style without it.
News Center items follow AP style for dates: abbreviate Jan., Feb., Aug., Sept., Oct., Nov. and Dec. with a specific date (Oct. 6, 2026); spell out March through July; lowercase seasons (fall 2024).
Times use a.m. and p.m. with no :00 for on-the-hour times (10 a.m.-2 p.m.).
Phone numbers use hyphens, no parentheses: 817-272-2101.
Rankings use No. in running text: No. 1, not #1.
Alumni get a parenthetical after the name: last two digits of the year and degree, most recent first -- e.g. ('99 PhD, '94 MS, Physics).
Arlington, Dallas, Fort Worth, and other well-known local cities need no state name; otherwise spell out the state.

audiences.label: Prospective undergraduates
audiences.description: High school students and transfer students deciding where to apply; many are first-generation.

audiences.label: Prospective graduate students
audiences.description: Working professionals and recent graduates comparing programs, cost, and format.

audiences.label: Parents and families
audiences.description: Supporting a student's decision; care about cost, safety, and outcomes.

audiences.label: Current students
audiences.description: Need a task done: register, pay, find a deadline or an office.

audiences.label: Faculty and staff
audiences.description: Internal readers who know the institution; want policy and process detail.

audiences.label: Alumni and donors
audiences.description: Connected to UTA; respond to impact stories and specific outcomes.

audiences.label: Media
audiences.description: Reporters and editors who need the facts, a quote, and a contact quickly.

audiences.label: Community and general public
audiences.description: Arlington and Dallas-Fort Worth residents, partners, and visitors.

examples.before: Discover a world of opportunities at UTA, a top-ranked university where you can unlock your potential and take your future to the next level.
examples.after: The University of Texas at Arlington is a Carnegie R-1 research university in the heart of the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex. In fall 2024, 49% of undergraduates had their full tuition and fees covered by financial aid.
examples.why: Replaces three generic AI phrases and an unsourced superlative with two verified facts from the knowledge base; full name on first reference.

examples.before: UTA is super excited to announce amazing enrollment growth this fall!
examples.after: Fall 2024 enrollment at The University of Texas at Arlington reached 41,613 students, with undergraduate enrollment up 3% from the previous year.
examples.why: News leads with the fact, not the feeling. Slang and exclamation removed; the figure comes from the University's own release.

examples.before: Learn more about UTA admissions. Apply today!
examples.after: Apply to UT Arlington: deadlines, requirements, and financial aid for first-year and transfer students, all in one place.
examples.why: Says what the page lets the reader do, within 155 characters, with no claims that need a source.
Verb-first and specific about what happens next; "click here" also fails screen-reader link lists.

open_questions.question: Serial comma: the University editorial guide requires it, but News Center items follow strict AP style without it.
open_questions.recommendation: Use the serial comma everywhere except the news-story and press-release templates.

open_questions.question: How and when to use Mavericks / Maverick in copy is not covered by the seed sample.
open_questions.recommendation: Use it only where the source material or brief already does, until the MME brand standards are added to this profile.
